readerCopy.body: A rule can be called non-negotiable at the exact moment the cost of obeying it becomes harder to justify. When Saturn opposes Lilith, authority and refusal face each other directly through rules, contracts, roles, or expectations that may still matter but no longer feel neutral. The pressure builds around arrangements that ask the person with less power to keep paying the same price. Some limits protect something worth keeping; others survive because challenging them has been more expensive than complying. The difference becomes clearer once the purpose of the rule and the cost of obedience are counted together.
